subject: Mathematics
chapterName: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates

questions.topic: Page 5: 1.3 THE 2-D CARTESIAN COORDINATE SYSTEM (Pages 5-6 Focus)
questions.questionText: In the floor plan represented by Fig 1.3, a designer needs to place a new window of exactly 3.5 units in width, starting at the coordinate x = 2.0. If the window is represented by a line segment on the x-axis, determine the coordinate of the endpoint of this window and explain the mathematical relationship between the segment length and the coordinate system.
questions.correctAnswer: The window will span from x = 2.0 to x = 5.5. The endpoint is at 5.5, calculated by adding the width (3.5) to the starting coordinate (2.0).
questions.explanationAnswer: The length of a horizontal segment on the x-axis is defined by the absolute difference between its endpoints: |x2 - x1| = length. Given the start point x1 = 2.0 and length = 3.5, we solve 3.5 = |x2 - 2.0|. Since the window extends forward, x2 = 2.0 + 3.5 = 5.5.
questions.explanationQuestion: This question reverses the process of finding a length from coordinates to finding a coordinate from a specified length, requiring an understanding of the additive property of segments on a Cartesian axis.

subjective_evaluation_points.point: Correctly identifying the starting coordinate x1 = 2.0 and the window width = 3.5.
Applying the mathematical relationship: Length = |x2 - x1|.
Providing a clear explanation of the additive property of segments on the coordinate axis.
